Gemini's UNVERIFIED_SOURCE_BLOCKED status for oscars.org was honest, not overclaimed; resolvable via these alternates.
2. cinema-people-005 (Bong Joon-ho, Best Director 92nd Oscars): CORRECT. Confirmed via Seattle Times/Consequence; beat Mendes/Scorsese/Phillips/Tarantino. Same oscars.org block, same resolution.
3. cinema-people-013 (Gary Oldman as Dracula, 1992): CORRECT. Cast mapping (Ryder=Mina, Hopkins=Van Helsing, Reeves=Harker) matches IMDb/Fandom cross-check.
4. cinema-people-021 (Mastroianni as journalist, La Dolce Vita): CORRECT. Wikipedia/BFI confirm Marcello Rubini is a tabloid journalist. Gemini's "editorial concern" (character forename matches option text) is a fair observation, not an error.
5. music-people-001 (Aretha Franklin, first woman in Rock Hall, 1987): CORRECT, confirmed via History.com/AmericanSongwriter/Britannica independent of rockhall.com.
6. music-people-005 (I Will Always Love You → Porter Wagoner): CORRECT, confirmed via Wikipedia/Newsweek.
7. music-people-013 (Freddie Mercury born Farrokh Bulsara): CORRECT, confirmed via Wikipedia/Biography.com.
8. music-people-021 (Sister Rosetta Tharpe, Gospel Train incl. Jericho + Precious Memories): CORRECT, Discogs/Wikipedia tracklist confirms both tracks on this album.

No factual or answer-key errors found in any of the 8 items; binding-check.json key/revision matches also hold.

One real but minor quality issue the report understates: its per-item "heuristics" character-length ranges are imprecise, e.g. item 1 claims options span "13–19 characters" but actual Cyrillic counts span 11–20; item 3 claims "10–14" but actual span is 10–15. Not an answer error, but the report states this as a checked fact with false precision — flag for correction, not rework.
